# What DigitalOcean tokens the library redacts, and what it leaves alone.
#
# Every token here is built from the ordered run 0123456789abcdef, which no real
# credential is: a body is sixty-four lowercase hexadecimal characters, so the
# run four times over is one, and the seven character prefix in front brings a
# token to seventy-one. Where a case turns on what a body may close on, its last
# character is written as a d instead.

patterns: digitalocean-token

# The three prefixes DigitalOcean writes a token with, one to a kind: dop_v1_
# for the personal access token generated in the control panel, doo_v1_ for the
# access token an application receives from the OAuth flow, dor_v1_ for the
# refresh token handed out beside it. They are one pattern because a caller with
# reason to redact any of them has the same reason for the rest, and the cases
# below are the three of them in the places a token is written.

case:     a personal access token in an environment assignment
in:       DIGITALOCEAN_TOKEN=dop_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      DIGITALOCEAN_TOKEN=«digitalocean-token»

case:     a token in the header a request carries it in
in:       Authorization: Bearer dop_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      Authorization: Bearer «digitalocean-token»

case:     an access token and the refresh token the oauth flow returns beside it
in:       {"access_token":"doo_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef","refresh_token":"dor_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"}
out:      {"access_token":"«digitalocean-token»","refresh_token":"«digitalocean-token»"}

case:     a token in the file the cli writes it into
in:       access-token: dop_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      access-token: «digitalocean-token»

case:     a token in the command line a request is made from
in:       curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer dop_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef' https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/account
out:      curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer «digitalocean-token»' https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/account

# The alphabet the sixty-four characters are written in: lowercase hexadecimal,
# which is what every token DigitalOcean's documentation, its CLI's tests and
# its Go client print behind the prefix. The prefix is read in one case as well,
# and the pattern's own file weighs what reading the uppercase shape would cost.
# What the alphabet leaves out is everything else, the letters past f and the two
# characters base64url adds among them, so a run carrying any of those is no
# token.

case:     an uppercase body
in:       dop_v1_0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      dop_v1_0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF

case:     an uppercase prefix
in:       DOP_V1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      DOP_V1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a letter past f in the body
in:       dop_v1_0123456789abcdefg123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      dop_v1_0123456789abcdefg123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a body carrying a hyphen
in:       dop_v1_0123456789abcdef-123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      dop_v1_0123456789abcdef-123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a body carrying an underscore
in:       dop_v1_0123456789abcdef_123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      dop_v1_0123456789abcdef_123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

# The lengths either side of sixty-four. That count is what DigitalOcean's own
# CLI demands, which accepts a token of seventy-one characters and nothing else,
# and it is used as a count rather than a floor: sixty-three characters are not
# a token, and sixty-five are a token and one character that belongs to no
# credential. The second of those is the price of having no boundary behind the
# match — a boundary there would drop this token rather than trim it, and a real
# token written against a hexadecimal character would come through whole.

case:     a body of sixty-four characters is a token
in:       dop_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «digitalocean-token»

case:     a body of sixty-three characters is not
in:       dop_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde
out:      dop_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde

case:     a hexadecimal run longer than a token is a token and what follows it
in:       dop_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0
out:      «digitalocean-token»0

# What a token may be written against. The prefix is the whole of the anchor and
# there is no boundary on either side of it, so a token keeps its span whatever
# word character it abuts.

case:     a token after an underscore
in:       DIGITALOCEAN_TOKEN_dop_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      DIGITALOCEAN_TOKEN_«digitalocean-token»

case:     a token after a letter
in:       xdop_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      x«digitalocean-token»

case:     a token before a hyphenated word
in:       dop_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef-suffix
out:      «digitalocean-token»-suffix

case:     a token at the end of a sentence
in:       the token is dop_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef.
out:      the token is «digitalocean-token».

case:     a token between tabs
in:       field\tdop_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef\tnext
out:      field\t«digitalocean-token»\tnext

case:     a token followed by crlf
in:       DIGITALOCEAN_TOKEN=dop_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef\r\n
out:      DIGITALOCEAN_TOKEN=«digitalocean-token»\r\n

case:     a token between multi-byte text with nothing between them
in:       日本語dop_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef日本語
out:      日本語«digitalocean-token»日本語

# Two tokens written together. A token can begin inside another at one position
# and no other: the o of an opening is no hexadecimal character, so the two
# letters a prefix opens with cannot both fall inside a body, and no character of
# a prefix past its first is a d, so no prefix begins inside another prefix
# either. What is left is a body closing on a d, with the rest of the next
# prefix written past the end of the token that d belongs to. The two spans
# overlap there and are redacted as one. Written without that overlap the two
# are separate values and both go, and a prefix standing where a body would have
# to hold it ends the candidate in front of it and opens the token itself.

case:     two tokens with nothing between them
in:       dop_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefdoo_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «digitalocean-token»«digitalocean-token»

case:     a token beginning at the last character of the token before it
in:       dop_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdedop_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «digitalocean-token»

case:     a prefix written where a body would stand
in:       dop_v1_dop_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      dop_v1_«digitalocean-token»

case:     one token of each kind, one per line over three lines
in:       dop_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef\ndoo_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef\ndor_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «digitalocean-token»\n«digitalocean-token»\n«digitalocean-token»

# What this pattern redacts that nobody issued. A SHA-256 is sixty-four
# lowercase hexadecimal characters and a body is exactly that, so the prefix and
# a digest is a token with nothing left over to tell the two apart. That is the
# answer rather than a fault in it, because sparing it would spare a real token:
# the vendor's format is that prefix and that many of those characters, and no
# part of it is left for a digest to fail. The same goes for a word ending in
# one of the three kinds with a version segment and a digest behind it: doo
# closes voodoo, and there the redaction begins at the fourth character and
# leaves the three in front of it in the text, which is what declining a word
# boundary in front costs. The digests shorter than the count are turned away by
# the count, and a base64url run can hold a prefix where standard base64 and
# hexadecimal cannot — those write no underscore.

case:     a sha-256 behind the prefix
in:       dop_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «digitalocean-token»

case:     a sha-1 behind the prefix
in:       dop_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      dop_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     an md5 behind the prefix
in:       dop_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      dop_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     the prefix inside a longer base64url run
in:       payload=zzzzdop_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefzzzz
out:      payload=zzzz«digitalocean-token»zzzz

case:     a word closing on the kind an oauth access token is named by
in:       voodoo_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      voo«digitalocean-token»

case:     a standard base64 payload, which carries no underscore
in:       payload=MIIBIjANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAAOCAQ8AMIIBCgKCAQEAdopv10123456789abcdef
out:      payload=MIIBIjANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAAOCAQ8AMIIBCgKCAQEAdopv10123456789abcdef

# And what this pattern leaves alone. The first three are the prefix, read with
# the version DigitalOcean writes and the underscores either side of it; the
# fourth is a kind DigitalOcean publishes no prefix for, which GitHub's secret
# scanning list names and the vendor documents nowhere. Then a body a space has
# broken, and two inputs carrying no prefix at all: a body holds no space and no
# punctuation, and the prefix closes on an underscore, so a word cannot run into
# one.

case:     a version digitalocean has not written
in:       dop_v2_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      dop_v2_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     hyphens where the version carries its underscores
in:       dop-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      dop-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     the version without the underscore that opens it
in:       dopv1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0
out:      dopv1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0

case:     a kind digitalocean names no prefix for
in:       dos_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      dos_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a body broken by a space
in:       dop_v1_0123456789abcdef 123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      dop_v1_0123456789abcdef 123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a run of the right length opening with no prefix
in:       xxx_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      xxx_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     prose
in:       there is no credential in this sentence
out:      there is no credential in this sentence

# And two shapes a reader auditing this pattern against DigitalOcean's own pages
# meets. The first is what the OAuth reference prints: both of the tokens on that
# page are seventy-one characters, which is what makes them worth reading for the
# width, and both carry EXAMPLE written over the front of the body — uppercase
# letters no hexadecimal string holds, so neither printed string is a value and
# neither is located. The second is the token DigitalOcean issued before the
# prefixes arrived, which its CLI still accepts: sixty-four characters with
# nothing in front of them, which is a SHA-256's format exactly. Those tokens
# were not revoked, so one reaching a log stays in the output whole; reading them
# would mean redacting every digest a caller passes through.

case:     the shape the documentation prints its examples in
in:       dop_v1_EXAMPLE789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      dop_v1_EXAMPLE789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     the token format this one replaced
in:       DIGITALOCEAN_TOKEN=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      DIGITALOCEAN_TOKEN=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a log line naming the api a token authenticates against
in:       time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="calling api" url=https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/account
out:      time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="calling api" url=https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/account
